takeoff.name: Sospel - Agaisen
takeoff.takeoff_description: The Agaisen launch, which faces SW, is perfect for going XC from. The locals call it \'The Lift\', for its large, regular thermals, and people have flown to Saint-Andre from here (appx 75km).
takeoff.going_there:
Sospel is most easily reached from the Menton exit of the A8 along the D2566, but you could also take the RD2204 from Nice.
Mt Agaisen: Once in Sospel, take the road signposted to the college. A left turning from this road climbs to Mont Agaisen. The road is tarmaced or concreted all the way to the top, and is suitable for all vehicles.
takeoff.comments:
Sospel is 40km (30 minutes) NE of Nice, or 15 minutes from Menton. It lies in the heart of the Bevera valley, protected by a cirque of mountains which surround it. It is very close to both the borders of the Mercantour National park, and of Italy. You are not allowed to fly in the National park itself (unless you are more than 1000m above the ground!), and this rule is taken very seriously by park wardens.
The views from on high are amazing: Mont Mangiabo to the north, Italy to the east and the Mediterranean Sea to the south. On a clear day you can see the point of Saint Tropez to the west.

takeoff.name: Gourdon
takeoff.takeoff_description: L'embarnier - a SE-facing rugged ridge, actually two takeoffs, a small one right next to the parking with a big rock in its midst, another one, large and easy, reachable by a short walk up the ridge.
takeoff.flight_rules:
This site is below the Nice Airport airspace, limiting it to FL65, so stay below 2000m.
More prohibited airspace (Nice and Cannes CTRs) towards the sea, to the south of the Valettes landing.
takeoff.comments:
Gourdon is 20km from the sea as the crow flies (and about 37km by road). The ridge reaches 1250m at its highest point, and has two take-offs, the upper of which is slightly bigger, both facing south-east. Because of the sea breeze, there is often dynamic lift to augment the thermic lift, and cross-countries are possible all year round. Convergence often sets up right over the site. The SE orientation means that you can launch early, and local pilots often leave Gourdon and reach Col de Bleyne just as that site is beginning to work.
You can drive all the way to take-off (carefully!) on a rough track, and top land, making it a very convenient site. It is also very popular, which makes it relatively easy to hitch back up to the top, but also means it can be very crowded at weekends.
takeoff.weather:
Although SE-facing, this site is protected by the sea breeze and is generally flyable even with a moderate NW,N or NE meteo wind above.
The site can be turbulent in a strong northerly meteo wind. Southerly wind reinforces the sea breeze.
In spring/summer, conditions usually get quite strong at midday, but that is lunch time anyway.

Valettes, in the distance below Bar s/Loup. Usually unreachable in summer due to strong valley winds, this is used commonly in winter for extended sled rides, this landing is suitable for hang gliders.
Top landing, either on takeoff itself (easy on the upper one, tricky on the parking one) or on the old roman track on the plateau behind the parking takeoff.
Outlandings are tricky (urbanized area to the south).

takeoff.name: Cagnorina - Tende- Tenda
takeoff.takeoff_description:
From Tende, take the road for La Pia, and follow the 'Parapente' signs to take-off. (This is about a 15 minute drive). You will pass a stadium on the way up, which can be used as a landing area in early mornings or evenings, but becomes too turbulent for use during the day.
Col de Tende: Turn immediately left after the Tende tunnel on the N204. Cross the '3 Amis' station, and climb up to the col on a good road (30 minutes from Tende).
takeoff.going_there: From Nice, take the A8 east to Ventimiglia, and join the N204 through the Gorges de Saorge to Tende.
takeoff.comments:
Tende is at the end of the Roya valley, about 50km north of Nice. It lies very close to the boundaries of the Mercantour national Park, which must not be overflown by paraglider (except at >1000m AGL).
There are two main sites: Cagnorina is just above the town itself, and Col de Tende is a few kilometres north of Tende, right on the Italian border. The col can be flown on either the south or the north sides.

takeoff.name: Monaco- Roquebrune- Mont Gros
takeoff.takeoff_description:
Leave the A8 at La Turbie, and follow the signs for the Monte Carlo golf club. Turn right at the Monte-Carlo radio antennae. Parking is limited (10 places) and hitching back up for a vehicle difficult. It makes sense to use the navette (euro1), which leaves from the car park opposite the train station (close to the landing area) between 10am and 4pm (10am, 11.15, 14.00 15.15 - only Oct-April). BEWARE OF FLYING RESTRICTIONS ( NOTAM, ZIT MENTON) ALWAYS CHECK Roquebrunailes website or fb BEFORE TAKING OFF.
If you see white waves on the see, just don't take off or if you are already flying, go to the landing quick.
takeoff.flight_rules:
local by-law, 2020. take off open to: - people older than 16 years, - school's students with 2 official instructors (one at take off, one at landing) - pilote with at least parapro4/ippi4 - glide with a wing loading below 5kg/m² (mini wing forbidden, if you are a test pilote you can ask the club for derogation)
site open: November 15 to April 30 : without restrictions. May 1st to June 30 : before 8h and after 18h (possible changes to better autorisation, check updates on Roquebrunaile website regularly) July 1st to August 31 : before 8h and after 19h. September 1st to Sept 30 : before 8h and after 18h. October 1st to November 15 : after 11h15.
Pilots on the take-off area must to be ready to fly. Use the surface of preparation to connect your glide with harness, or other.
Flight above take-off forbidden.
Top-landing only on the main take-off.
Professionals instructors must: - be in rule with 'jeunesse et sport' ministry, - have a professional insurance, - have a authorization from the town hall.
fly above houses: more than 100m;
fly above military base forbidden;
Acro and SIV maneuvers forbidden; more informations (french local club): http://www.roquebrunailes.com/en/regulation-roquebrune.htm
Max Altitude: 1981m/amsl or max 305 above ground!!!! See map here: http://www.roquebrunailes.com/en/free-flighing-alpes-maritimes.htm

landing.landing_description: From takeoff, follow the road back down to La Turbie and turn left at the main road. Follow this road until the junction where you see the big, dominant hotel. Take a sharp right hand turn back on yourself at this junction. Follow this road to the T-junction, where you turn left. Follow this road, and go straight across at the first set of traffic lights, crossing the main road, into a smaller road opposite. Follow this road round the valley. At the other side, take the right-hand turn that is signposted for the railway station. Drive down this road to the bridge over the railway. The road then goes left to the station - park around here, and take the steps on the right-hand side down to the beach.

takeoff.name: Greolieres
takeoff.takeoff_description:
The main (lower) take-off is a 30 min walk from GrÃ©oliÃ¨res village. The school runs a navette service (from 9 am) to this or to the upper TO in summer. Ski station chair lifts from the resort of GrÃ©oliÃ¨res-les-Neiges can be used to access this upper take-off in winter.

takeoff.comments:
With a high-point of 1770m, the Cheiron is the biggest and most obvious ridge in this area (Look out for it as you fly over on the approach to Nice airport!). It is a very reliable site, with year-round thermals pulling the air up the front even when the clouds are scooting over the top from the north (but be prepared to encounter this wind if you fly above cliff height). It offers both dynamic lift and thermals all year round.
In terms of XC, it is not the easiest site to get away from, but there is a straight-forward 15km out-and-return ridge-run to Coursegoules that is very achievable on a reasonable day. The accessibility of the site, and that it is so often flyable, coupled with the magnificent views of Mediterranean, the snow-capped Mercantour and the ski-slopes on the north side of the mountain are reason enough to fly here for most!.
Informations from http://www.flyozone.com/paragliders/de/infozone/fly-gourdon/greolieres/

takeoff.name: Thorenc - Col de Bleyne
takeoff.takeoff_description:
alti:1525m Approximately 400m top to bottom.
Beware of snagging lines on stones / shrubs on take-off. The wind can switch direction slightly, making launching a little tricky if you catch it at the wrong moment.
takeoff.flight_rules: Be careful, take off is very near the Nice TMA.
takeoff.going_there:
From Nice, head east along the A8 and take the Cagnes sur Mer exit. Then either follow the D6 from la Colle sur Loup to GrÃƒÂ©oliÃƒÂ¨res through the Gorges du Loup, or come through Vence and via Coursegoules on the D236 and then the D2. From GrÃƒÂ©oliÃƒÂ¨res, take the road to Thorenc and climb up to the Col de Bleyne. At the Col, a track breaks off right and goes all the way to take-off.
The take-off you see is CDB1 (for these purposes - not an official name). To get to CDB2 there is a short walk on a path through the trees to the east.
takeoff.comments:
The site record is held by David Dagault for a 257km flight to Megeve on 8th May 1998. Col de Bleyne is a southerly-facing site with a 400m top-to-bottom and excellent XC potential. There are an abundance of big fields to land in both in its own valley, and along the route to Saint AndrÃƒÂ©, although in spring and early summer grass is grown as crop, and fields containing it should be avoided. The Montagne de Thorenc is best flown in a light southerly meteo wind direction, although on a good, light-wind day thermals will be drawn up the front regardless.
The site is primarily a thermic site, so is most often used in Spring and summer, although people have been known to thermal there above snow-covered fields in winter!
Informations from http://www.flyozone.com/site_guide/cdb.asp

alti: 2274m The summit of Cime de la Bercha can be gained via a cable car from St Etienne de TinÃ©e, or by a rough track from Auron.
Las Donnas is reachable by a cable car from Auron. It is on the south side of Auron, so in the mornings when you can launch facing N or E you can land in the Auron valley, but once it becomes thermic you\'ll be on the south side of the mountain. It is easy to land in the small village of Roya, which is served by a road (the D61), but advisable to arrange a retrieve before doing so!
The cable cars work all winter, and also in July and August.

Follow this north (towards Digne) until it joins the D2205 at the entrance to the Gorges de la Mescla. From here, take the D2205, signed Isola and Auron, all the way to Auron and St Etienne de TinÃ©e.
takeoff.comments:
Auron is a mountain village about 90km NNW of Nice, which is very popular as a winter ski resort. It sits in a little pocket that is not included in the Parc National du Mercantour. It is just south of the town of St Etienne de TinÃ©e, on the D2205. La Cime de la Berchia (2270m) is the principal launch site of Auron, providing a good high-altitude launch point which can be reached by cable car in winter, or by track, with great cross country potential.
Note that paragliding and other aerial sports are banned in the National park itself (unless you are at an altitude of greater than 1000m above the ground) so be aware of its borders.
Weather information is posted in the cable car station and the St Etienne de TinÃ©e tourist office.

takeoff.name: Déco Baisse de Raymond (Veillos)
takeoff.takeoff_description:
There are several take-offs at La Colmiane, but the most often used are the two described below:
Veillos There are actually two south-facing 'Veillos' launches, that are located on spines of the Mont PÃ©toumier - Mont PÃ©poiri ridge north of La Colmiane. All summer there is a Navette from the Veillos chairlift, and the chairlift itself is in use.You can also drive up:
From La Colmiane, head out on the D2565 towards St Dalmas. On the very first sharp left-hand U-bend in the road, there is a minor road that goes straight. Take this. It immediately splits into two forks, the right-hand one of which is the track up to take-off. (There is a chain across the bottom - replace this after you). You pass 2 hang-glider launches as you zig-zag up the hillside, and the road eventually flattens out and goes into the back of the bowl. Continue here, going left on the main track when the road goes right to a refuge. The road follows the ridge-line to its end, and then zig-zags up again. You can park at the top of the zig-zags. Take-off is the grassy area above the road.
Le Pic de Colmiane From the col at la Colmiane, drive up the dirt track that goes to Col du Suc, which is signed 'Parapente'. Drive past the first streamered area - the better takeoff is higher up. You can park in the obvious area where the road goes over the col, and walk up the footpath which goes to the top of the chairlift. Launch is just below the chairlift, and is a clear, grassy area marked by windsocks.
takeoff.going_there: D2205. 5 km before St Saveur de TinÃ©e, turn off on the D2565 on the right, which goes to La Colmiane. You reach the small village of St Dalmas about 2km before arriving at La Colmiane ski station. The football field in St Dalmas, known as 'Le Soun Pra', is the official landing field, and is signposted from the village. Libuelle, the paragliding school, have a bulletin board on their building in the landing field. This shows the locations of the main take-offs and landings.
takeoff.comments:
La Colmiane lies south of the boundary to the Mercantour National Park, approximately 40km almost directly north of Nice. It is within easy reach of the large mountains to the North and the views once high are spectacular, reaching into Italy.
informations from http://www.flyozone.com/site_guide/colmaine.asp
takeoff.weather: Beware that wind can easily switch from coming up to coming over the back of the col above the main landing therefore you should check the wind direction on approach. The valley is also pretty well protected but the surrounding valeys are narrow, this should be taken into account if leaving the area and flying XC

takeoff.name: Superbagneres - luchon
takeoff.takeoff_description: Drive to the ski sation, outside the times that the ski lift doesn't run. Otherwise, take the lift, take off is immediately on the left on the slope next to the derelict church. Steep, but easy. Wind will be light so forward is needed sometimes.

Absolutely Amazing flying. Ask a Pro for advice. Close to an airfield, regulated flying for landing approach. Please read the posted guidelines on the notice board.
If you are experienced enough, in the afternoon, when the breeze eases off a little, you can cross to the other side of the valley, soaring 'the road' all the way up and then plenty of possibilities to make it far enough into the valley against the wind. Take care, serious turbulence is possible.
takeoff.weather: Southwind is dangerous. Lots of turbulence. Strong valley wind in the afternoon. Fly Lac d'Oo instead and come back evening for a nice valley wind soar.

takeoff.name: La Seranne - Déco France
takeoff.takeoff_description: Décollage pour le parapente et un pour le deltaplane. Vent : S et SE/SO Ne pas se jeter dans la sellette. Bien penser à courrir courrir et encore courrir. S'attendre a un thermique en sortie de déco. Et donc faire une tempo / coup de frein. Tenir sa voile.
takeoff.flight_rules: Altitude max : 3500 mètres QNH le week-end Bien prendre et garder du gaz. Ne pas passer en dessous de la vierge. Cela rend très difficile le retour vers l'atterro officiel. Vers le Pic Baudile, autour de Saint Jean de Buèges. Restez au relief. Ne pas descendre en vallée. Une zone de protection rapaces est autour de Saint Jean de Bueges.
takeoff.going_there:
Montpellier : direction Ganges. Turn in Cazilhac-Le-Haut then take a dirt road for 40 minutes.
There is a shuttle going to the take-off site once per day on most days that are flyable. The shuttle usually leaves around 13h from Coupiac (the landing spot). The shuttle is operated by the club 'Les ailes de la Seranne'. To see if the shuttle is running on a particular day, post to the discussion thread here or contact the club.
It is also possible to walk up to the takeoff site, either by the road or using one of several footpaths. You should count 1 or 1.5 hours, depending on your condition.
http://les-ailes-de-la-seranne.fr/
takeoff.comments:
This is a magnificent site, probably one of the best in the region.
Good XC site
takeoff.weather: You can fly with N and NW wind but it can be strong suddenly so be careful. Tune your radio to the frequency 143.98.75 to hear the updated wind information broadcast every 10 minutes

landing.landing_description:
The main landing spot is 6 km to the north-east following the mountain in 'Coupiac' (this is the prefered landing spot, and is also the pickup point for the shuttle).
If landing in Coupiac is not possible a backup landing spot is just at the bottom of the takeoff (direction NE) at a site called 'Les Prats'

Walking acces about 15-20 minutes

takeoff.name: Reinhardsmunster
takeoff.takeoff_description:
460 meters. When arriving in Reinhardsmunster turn left onto the road to Obersteigen. 1 km later, GO STRAIGHT AHEAD and follow the forest road which leads to a car park at an intersection (6 km). Once parked turn south and you can choose one of 2 paths that lead to the takeoff. The main one is the one behind the wooden ramp/gate: walk 100m along a forest road then there's a small path going right and diagonally up the hill for another 100m to the takeoff. There's an INFO PANEL just as you arrive, READ IT :) An alternative path from the parking is parallel and above the first one. It starts 20m to the west of the ramp. Always stay left and when you exit the forest and walk another 50m you'll see the takeoff on your left.
Large and relatively easy take off. A bit steep, covered with astroturf(carpet). Slippery when wet!
Landing on the right not visble until you take off.
For HG landing is better on the left, at the practice area/spot. Can be seen from the takeooff.
takeoff.flight_rules: Airspace during the weekdays: YOU MUST contact the Phalsbourg airbase (Tél. 03 87 25 21 53) !!! if you are the fist OR last to fly/land!!! see airspace image in the PHOTOS. Do not take off after 30 minutes prior to sunset. In september (ususally the whole month) the site is CLOSED due to the "Brame du Cerf" the annual deer breeding time. Check with the local pilots and/or contact numbers on the Flying site information pannel (on the takeoff and landing).
takeoff.comments:
XC to Haut Barr castle (up north) is a classic.
Max. height : 1520m
Flights are NOT ALLOWED from monday 06h00 friday 15h00 (military zone).
Access to the site is strictly FORBIDDEN in September (deers fornication ...).
takeoff.weather:
Take off a very technical, can be dangerous, in strong wind.
Magic lift fenomenon on some days in the evening.

takeoff.name: Montlambert
takeoff.takeoff_description: alti: 890m after 12h thermals and breeze can be strong. Lot's of pilots come here, we thank you to drive slowly and respect the people living on the road to the launch area. This site is fragile! If people complain too much we might lose the right to fly here. So don't unload your car at the turning point on top. Do it when parked further down the road. Respect nature, the people and regulations!
takeoff.going_there: Landing area: from Montmelian, take the N6 road. Turn to the left to 'Saint Jean de la Porte'. Before 'St Jean' turn to the left just after passing a bridge and go along a canal during 1 km. You have to cross a small bridge again. Take off from landing area: at the end of the dirt road turn left. In 'Saint Jean de la Porte' turn left. After 1 or 2 km turn to the right, to Montlambert. In Montlambert turn back and and park your car, but not in the village! Walk 10 mn to the Southwest.
takeoff.comments: This site is closed between mid September to beginning of November, because of an agreement with the local hunters. It is their best moment of joy, so again respect their fun as they do ours! Please inform yourselves about exact days of no-flying. On some days flying is still allowed.
takeoff.weather: With North wind : The only site (with Courtet) where you can fly around Grenoble. But be careful with strong North wind (above ~20km/h) it's just a little protection and the wind can come quite suddenly. Also be careful when flying over ~1400m, the upper mountain protection can stop and you can find turbulences due to being on the lee side. With SW wind or W wind, the take off is on the lee side of the takeoff's West side crest, if wind speed is low (below 10km/h) it might still be okay but not by stronger SW or W wind. With W wind it's flyable, but it might be uncomfortable because of turbulences far above the valley. In doubt, meet pilots on the site for advices.

takeoff.takeoff_description: alti:1150m after 13h the breeze is coming. Thermic during the afternoon, great flight at the end of the day, over the Aiguebelette lake.
takeoff.going_there: from Chambéry take the highway to Lyon. After the 'L'Épine' tunnel go out (Novalaise/Lac d'Aiguebelette, exit n°12). First crossroad on your left, and another time left immediately. Landing is just behind trees. To go on the takeoff go to the 'col de l'Épine' pass with the D916 road. Just before the pass turn on your left and take a road on 3 km. Follow 'décollage' advertising.
takeoff.comments: good for child, there is a beautiful lake just near the site. No wind and hot water.
takeoff.weather: The takeoff is under the wind if it's coming from the North, NE, E or SE. Still flyable and possible to takeoff by North moderate wind (bellow 15km/h) but be careful by higher wind. By any East component of wind you might find a gentle West breeze at takeoff to let you believe it is fine. Be extra careful, check the wind sock on tree top. You might be able to take off anyway but your flight might be rough and very uncomfortable (even dangerous).

landing.landing_description: near the entrance to the highway, on your right. Be careful, this area is fragile. Pack your glide under the trees, near the parking. Conditions : Unless you happen to be there by strong Est wind ("Le Farou") where you might find uncomfortable lee side landing, it is rarely windy, its position makes it protected from most winds. This landing is also called "the Swamp", if you attempt landing during winter (January to March) you might be displeased by the 10 to 20cm mud waiting for you.

from 'Albertville', go to 'Les Saisies'. You can stop at the landing area. After go to 'Les Saisies' By car : turn to the left when you arrive in this ski station. Keep the road to the end, there is an Altitude restaurant on the top. During winter or sping when there is still a lot of snow (up to around beginning of May), the road to the takeoff is unusable by car, but you can use the chairlift, there are one way tickets for paragliders. During summer (July and August) there are (in 2020 : free) buses that you can use from to go from the Valley (Beaufort or Villard sur Doron) to Les Saisies. Then you can use the chairlift (open in July and August) to reach the takeoff
More info somewhere on there site : https://www.lessaisies.com
In 2020 the information page is here (but it changes every now and then) : https://www.lessaisies.com/bus-albertville-navettes-intramuros-gratuites.html

It might happen that your arrive too late at this takeoff (like 12am or later) and the valley breeze is already blowing from the back (North) Then there is an alternate takeoff (check the map), that can also be used with North wind from which you can still takeoff and reach the south face (in the lee side). Discouraged with strong North wind !
A good idee to go to 'Aravis', in spring. Beaufortain is a good district for family holidays: a lots of differents activities. You can finish your day in 'Le Cormet de Roselend', a soaring site. You will fly until the night with the breeze!
takeoff.weather: Later in the day the breeze might be stronger than the thermals and be coming in your back.

takeoff.name: Plaine Joux (Passy)
takeoff.takeoff_description: At Plaine Joux. Wide take off, nicely prepared. Can be windy the afternoon (valley brise)
takeoff.flight_rules:
The cliff behind the takeoff is part of the national park - it is not allowed to fly closer than 300m from it. The cliff more to the to the west is OK to fly close.
At both landing sites the approach should be the standard 'C' approach, please respect this rule as the sky over the landing fields, especially Chedde, is often very crowded.
At landing sites the kiting should be interrupted when pilots are on the approach.
At the Marlioz landing site the hang gliders have got the prioriity on the approach.
ATTN: if flying towards Chamonix/ Mont Blanc: observe flight restrictions: no TO, landing and overflight! (>> see pix) > France - LF R30B: July-August - LF R30A: permanent > Italy: 4.8. - 15.9.2016
takeoff.going_there:
Getting to launch site: 1) by car, approx 15min drive up. If you are alone, try to ask around, possibly there may be other pilot(s) willing to go up, so one car you can keep at landing. 2) by shuttle. On the weekend days you can find some vans offering shuttle service, or if you are kind you can join the vans of tandem flights or school. 2020: Public bus (SAT) L85 is available to go to the take off: the bus stop is on Chedde market place. 3,5 € until Guébriant and 6 € until Plaine-Joux (about 950m walk after Guébriant stop) link to the L85 timetable: http://www.sat-montblanc.com/horaire-timetables/ligne-85-sallanches-plateau-d-assy-pleine-joux.aspx
3) Walking. It is approximately 1,5hr walk from the landing site of Chedde. Walk up to the road which goes to Servoz, then walk towards Servoz (1km) until find footpath with indicator to Plaine Joux. Then walk up.
takeoff.comments: Chedde landing site is usually more crowded, higher chances of getting shuttles from there.
takeoff.weather:
Avoid flying with strong west, south west wind. With west wind coming, the landing is hard to reach, and conditions can be really turbulent.
Very well protected from north wind. It is still flyable even with insane north wind.
Usually west wind is related to foehn. ALWAYS check Foehn before flying: VERY turbulent conditions if Foehn is NOT between -4 hPa and +4 hPa. Check foehn forecast on http://www.meteocentrale.ch/fr/meteo/foehn-et-bise/foehn.html

takeoff_parking.takeoff_parking_description: Huge parking just 100m from the launch site.

landing.landing_description:
Two landing sites exist: Chedde and Batistock, both just 1km apart.
Batistock site is much bigger and suitable for hang gliders. Chedde is smaller, more technical but still suitable for beginners.
Batistock site is on the way from Passy to Le Fayet (big field on the right, access from other side): 45°54'57''N - 06°42'21''E
Site identified on the map is the Chedde site.

takeoff.name: Agy plane
takeoff.takeoff_description: Strong Valley wind and thermic gusts. Nice grassy take off area, locals will be flying, read the FFVL site board-it's in French and English.
takeoff.flight_rules: delicate LZ! absolutely avoid out-landing!!
takeoff.going_there: From Cluses-> follow the signs to Les Gets/Morzine. at Chatillon-sur-Cluses, turn right at the sign: Saint-Sigismond. At the end of Saint-Sigismond- turn left and follow the road all the way up to Agy Plane, get to the top of the mountain road and there is a little bar/restaurant - go further up and park by the Radio Tower/Satellite building.
takeoff.comments:
Endless XC routes.
Acro : Known as Antoines secret training spot. Agy is the take off site above and to the side of the town Cluses. If training acro- the pilot has to make a short flight across from Agy to Chevran. Regardless of the met wind-the valley wind is sucked into Chamonix most good forecasted days when the sun shines, this valley wind displaces up Chevran Mountain in a mix of dynamic&thermic. Making it a mini magic mountain, Chevran is 600M high off the valley floor and in general a pilot on an acro wing would have anything from 600m to 800m vertical once pushing out from Chevran above Cluses. Beware of the diagonal drift towards the mountain in a maneuver. In a rescue situation the trees of Chevran would be the landing point but with a Rogallo, there is space to land below the foot of the Mountain.
takeoff.weather: 1 >Bise wind-that strong NE wind that ruins most valley winds can have some effect. 2 >When Northerlies mix with valley wind if forecasted to blow hard, only good for small wings. 3 >Thermic gusts from the town of Cluses when entering the lower level valley wind and a somewhat technical landing if you approach in the peak of the valley wind, nice and smooth landing later in the evening.

landing.landing_description: fly straight out from Chevran and about 500m into Cluses you will see a landing area marked with a big T on the grass, sometimes there are camper vans there so make the most of a safe area anywhere in the valley to land.

takeoff.name: Ste Anastasie
takeoff.takeoff_description:
Large take off place on the St Quinis massif. South side, visible from Landing place.
Possibility to land near the take off. Needs good skill of landing on small area. High trees all around.
Details here: https://tasie-parapente.club/le-site/
ONLY 4x4 vehicles can use the very bad track leading to take off.
takeoff.flight_rules:
WARNING !!! Site on a military zone where helicopters are flying a lot.
Flyable only if authorization is allowed by the military base. Info given everyday on the club website must be read before to go to the take off: https://tasie-parapente.club/le-site/
Normally, if our area is open, we must fly on the space allowed and limited to level 650m ASL above sea level) about 15m above highest relief summit of St Quinis.
Radio equipment is mandatory to fly here, tuned on FFVL frequency (143.9875 Mhz).
Thanks to respect those rules for maintaining the site flyable.
Local pilots will be happy to inform you.
takeoff.going_there:
Landing place is located on North side of Sainte Anastasie sur Issole village. Between railroad and St Quinis massif. Car-park available on the landing place.
Take off access walking on a stony path climbing to the relief (about 20Mn, 1000m distance, 180m level).

takeoff.name: Montgirod-Arcachat
takeoff.takeoff_description:
2000m When you are under the power lines along the road after the cheese farm- go to your right on a 4x4 track and make a judgement on where to launch from off the steeper slope
1900m (GPS co-ords) Normally use this launch on the far SW part of the mountain away from the power lines and easier to access. Go just past the refuge and look for the little wind streamer on the steeper gradient next to some small shrubs, park your car on the corner.
takeoff.going_there: From Moutiers take the N90 road, 'Bourg saint Maurice' direction. After the tunnel go into Centron, then up to 'Montgirod' direction. Go straight up past Montgirod on a little tar farmer road, park by the cheese farm where the tar road ends or go higher if your car can do so. It's about the same distance driving to launch as it is driving up to Forclaz(Annecy) from Doussard, meaning - roughly 15km from Centron to the launch.
takeoff.comments:
XC : This site starts to work early in the year as well as early in the morning. Facing SE with a very steep gradient that has little cow paddocks and forest getting that morning sun this site boasts some good thermalling opportunities. If the wind is N around to W, it is still possible to get flights in before 1pm thanks to its orientation and the micro climate of the Centon/Villette area. However when the valley system works it comes over the top joining the valley wind from Moutiers towards the high mountains from as early as 11am. BUT-It is possible to fly in the afternoon on a stable day trying to fly bubbles on the lee side especially in Autumn/Winter. Despite all meteo winds, every flight at about 10am, there is a light pleasant thermal breeze on launch, with a view of Tignes Grande Motte,Saint Foy,La Rosiere,les Arcs,la Plagne,Val Thorens,Meribel and Courchevel. There are various routes to take once gaining altitude with an early start to your day, some local French pilots have achieved massive distances and return triangles If you are unlucky with the wind or arrive too late-there is a small ridge to fly from that is a good XC starting point for afternoon flying behind the Montgirod side, the launch faces W called Naves.
ACRO : Beware : Centron houses and power lines and main road, fly acro over the trees in the left corner. Fly with a Rogallo or Base system. Minimum 700m in the box with bad wind, max 1000m starting at 1900m. The same distance driving to launch as driving up to Forclaz(Annecy) from Doussard, but the road is smaller, at least tar all the way up. The glide out to the 'box' can also be compared to Annecy at some (2.5 to 2.7km), this is good because most sites in the French Alps used to do 'acro ploufs' require a long glide that eats height.
takeoff.weather:
Spring and Autumn : Hunting season, do not go to the toilet in the trees up the mountain.
Summer: Venturi in the valley.
Winter : foehn wind days-you shouldn't be out there anyway.

takeoff.flight_rules: Stay out of the Vanoise National Park (to the South and South East) if flying XC.

takeoff.weather: Can get strong and bouncy in the middle of the afternoon, although rarely unflyable.

takeoff.name: Serres Beaumont
takeoff.takeoff_description: Good, early, in the morning, when the sun light the rocks which are just under the TV transmitter. WARNING : be very carefull before taking your decision => take off is under the north, the west and the south wind. WARNING : when east wind (other than brise) is facing the takeoff, it can be difficult to reach a comfortable landing. Be very carefull.
takeoff.going_there:
Option 1 : from MÃ©reuil, 10 minutes of car + 40 minutes by feet. Climb on the East side. goto the small village called MÃ©reuil. Arriving at MÃ©reuil, continue to climb in the direction of 'La Montagne'. Just before arriving at La Montagne, leave the main road and take the forest pist named B22. If the pist is closed by the fence, you must continue by feet. 4x4 recommended. Follow B22 during 2.5km until the end of the forest pist: there is a aera where you can make a u-turn and you can park the 4x4. Then by feet climb strait in the oak/beech forest during 30 minutes. At the end of the forest, it's a little bit hard. Even if it's harder, choose the right side of the slope because on the left side, the main trail is too close from the cliff and it really dangerous, especially if you carry your aisle on your back. Continue to climb 250m until you can see the other side of the mountain (west). You are arrived.
Option 2 now forbidden by ONF (130â‚¬ fine at your own risk): from Montclus, 40 minutes of 4x4 car, 5 minutes by feet. This option is easier that the MÃ©reuil one, but the road is much longer and is now forbidden. Arriving from Serres at Monclus, take on your left and climb, climb, and climb using the forest pist which comes to the TV Transmitter. 800m before arriving to the transmitter, park the car and walk 250m on the GR94 on the opposite way of the transmitter.
takeoff.weather: In the summer, avoid to flight after 12h00 in this area : take off can be smooth and ok while it can be very dangerous in the valley (strong brise, and too strong thermals).

takeoff.takeoff_description: The take-offs are quite short but do not present any particular difficulties.
takeoff.flight_rules:
A prefectoral decree regulates access to the Bouches du Rhône mountains during the summer period from 1 June to 30 September. In the orange period access is free, in the red period it is limited between 6am and 11am, and in the black period any penetration is strictly prohibited and punishable by a contravention. Information on 0811 20 13 13 13 or on the website http://www.bouches-du-rhone.pref.gouv.fr/index.php
Flights possible during the hunting season except on days when game is released (see calendar on the information panel on the website).
The site is located in the TMA Marseille Provence 6 (ceiling limited to 1370 m altitude (4500 feet).
takeoff.going_there: On the A501 motorway linking Marseille to Aix en Provence via Aubagne, exit at exit 7, join the big roundabout and take the D96 for about a hundred metres. Then take the Chemin des Solans to a small roundabout where you have to turn left to stay on the Chemin des Solans. At the end of this road, at the end of the paved road, you will find a dirt DFCI track on the right that leads to a dirt parking with two large green tanks. This is where you should stop and consult the Site information panel. (Geographical coordinates of the car park: N43°19'27.67" / E 5°33'31.93"). Access to the decos is by foot, it takes about 40 minutes to walk. Access to the landing by vehicle is strictly prohibited.
takeoff.comments: Presence of a quiet area for the protection of the Bonelli's eagle. This area does not apply to the site for local flight. It is located 5km from the takeoff, in the municipality of Gémenos, heading east. This type of "upwind" flight is unlikely and of no interest.
takeoff.weather:
General orientation: East to South. Dangerous in North, NW and NE winds and in Westerly winds. Favourable with easterly, east-south-easterly, south-south-easterly and south-south winds.
In breezy conditions and in the absence of strong weather winds, flight is possible in the middle of the morning. However, the southwest sea breeze returns fairly quickly at midday, more or less early depending on the season due to the proximity of the sea, making flying turbulent and inadvisable.

It will take you to the 'Pas de L'escalette'. 200m before getting there, you will see white fences boarding the trail. Make a left just before. It will take you off trail for 150m and get you to the take off. Don't expect to find it by yourself the first time, but you will likely see wings there.

People usually meet at the parking at around 5:30pm during summer.
A very technical site.

takeoff.name: le Chalvet (Saint Andre les Alpes)
takeoff.takeoff_description: The main launch SW/ W is relatively steep, and thermic from around midday. The wind on take-off can be strong, particularly later on when the valley winds become established. When the thermic activity dies down again, very pleasant evening soaring is often available until it gets dark. South-East launches are easy, very large.
takeoff.flight_rules: Groups and schools have to contact Aerogliss before coming. +33 492891130 or divers@aerogliss.com
takeoff.going_there: There is a good (but narrow) paved road (The C30) up to Le Chalvet take-off from the NW side of the town, but this is often snowed in from December to March. For parking, there is a lay-by close to the S take-off, and places for several cars at the end of the road beneath the South-West launch. The Lakeside landing area / Aerogliss HQ is reached by taking the road to Nice out of St Andre, and turning left by the supermarket. This link takes you to a local map up to take off and intro about the site: http://flystandre.com/flying-services/chalvet-site-intro/ Normally shuttle buses operate from the LZ.
takeoff.comments: St Andre is a well-known flying site, having been used for international paragliding and hang gliding events for years. It is renowned for its strong thermals and good cross country potential, with routes to the north to Dormillouse, Briancon, Allos etc, and south to Col de Bleyne. The main (SW) launch tends to blow out for paragliders when conditions get really thermic and the valley breezes get strong, so cross country-seekers need to aim to be on launch for 11:30 to 13:00, ready for the sun to begin pulling thermals up the SW face. For those seeking gentler conditions, there are E and SE-facing launches for morning flights, and evening flying until sunset from the SW launch can be very rewarding. There is a good road to top, but it is often snowed in during the winter (Dec to Mar). Note: St Andre is not an FFVL flying site. Aerogliss administer the site, and ask that all visiting pilots contact them before flying. (Their base is in next to the lakeside landing field. Contact details given below).
takeoff.weather: Lake landing can be turbulent in a rather strong N or NW meteo wind (Mistral). In fact, by light Mistral, no troubles by starting from the SW launch, but when conditions are getting only windy,we oftenly catch a microwave. with a light North, it is flyable too (North launch), but no real interest. Wind info (alos on FFVL frequency): http://www.balisemeteo.com/depart.php?dept=04 http://www.balisemeteo.com/balise.php?idBalise=109 For full access to all the Saint Andre weather including wind speed on launch etc on a single page visit: http://flystandre.com/webcam-weather/

takeoff.going_there: Depuis Besançon centre ville (Chamars), prendre la direction de Lyon. Environ 100 m avant le panneau de fin d'agglomération de Besançon, prendre le pont qui mène à Velotte. Prendre la rue à gauche à environ 100 m de la sortie du pont et suivre la rive droite du Doubs. Passer sous le pont de la N 273 et prendre tout de suite à droite. Suivre la direction du Fort de Planoise. Arrivé au fort, suivre la flèche « Emmaüs », vers la droite. Le décollage est juste en face.
takeoff.comments: Le site est très sain et facile, tant en parapente qu'en delta, par vent de Nord-Est qui est l'un des vents dominants dans la région. Cependant par vent de nord il faut se méfier des éventuels rouleaux dus à la côte située à gauche du décollage. De même par vent d'est des rouleaux peuvent apparaître, dus aux reliefs situés à l'est (Montfaucon notamment). Dans ces deux cas il faut rejoindre l'atterrissage des Craies en « sautant » la côte située à droite du décollage avant d'avoir perdu trop d'altitude ; l'atterrissage est juste derrière. Un atterrissage de dépannage peut être utilisé : le terrain de Base-Ball situé à gauche du décollage. En cas de gros problème il est possible de se poser dans une friche située à droite du terrain de Base Ball. Éviter les serres situées sous le décollage !

takeoff.name: Pignu
takeoff.comments: Le site du Pignu est situé côté golfe de Saint Florent avec un dénivelé de 900 mètres. Le Pignu est notre site privilégié pour les baptêmes parapente et pour les vols d’initiation en soirée. Les thermiques sont généreux en journée, avec la possibilité de voir la mer des 2 côtés du Cap Corse. En soirée, le site permet un vol calme avec un panorama magnifique devant les yeux. Aucune difficulté particulière ! Interdiction de survoler les antennes (zone militaire) ! Attention le site est situé dans la TMA3 de l’aéroport de Bastia Poretta (voir carte Carte TMA3). Accès au décollage : à partir de la route qui mène aux antennes du Pignu (route à droite à 500 mètres avant le Col de Teghjime en venant de Bastia).
